_about: Duda motion tokens. Measured from Duda's curated Rive files (reference/motion-extract.md) unless marked 'rule'. Units: ms, px at the 680-wide design frame unless noted.

canvas.about: Reference canvas (video 1). A project can set its own `canvas: {design, output}` in beats.yaml; px values in these tokens are then converted so they keep their size on the output (choreo.configure).

duda.use: house in-out: short moves of visible elements, scale, size, gradients

settle.use: arrive-and-settle: entrances (element appears while moving) and short repositions <= 60 px

scroll.use: long in-scene scrolls of readable content (a list, a table): the softer in-out peaks at ~2.5x its mean speed (duda: ~4x), so 800+ px stay under the 30 px/frame text cap
scroll.source: rule: video 2 (Copilot) table scroll; same curve as the measured 'gradient' ease

linear.use: opacity fades, cursor press/release, spinners, remap time only

closing_words.about: The closing line comes in word by word: each word fades in, rises and sharpens from a light blur. The first word starts delay_after_cut_ms after the closing scene's cut (its entry is still landing); the subline starts subline_gap_ms after the title's last word. Build the line with rvbuild `Video.words`, animate it with the `words` beat.
closing_words.blur_about: Feather strength at the start of each word, in px of the 680-wide reference (6 and 3.5 in a 1360 storyboard frame). Light: the first try (5 and 2.5) read as out of focus
closing_words.source: rule: user review of eComm v10 ('diminua o delay, um mínimo delay entre as palavras, um efeito leve de blur'), approved on v11 as the standard

cursor.source: hero_smb: cursors on Follow Path, enter from off-frame with cubicValue (0,0,0,0.10)-like fast starts, leave with (0.66,..,1.0,..) accelerating; pass points with nonzero speed; press 1 -> 0.83-0.87 in 4-5 frames. hero1: same press (0.85, 3 frames).
cursor.path: FollowPathConstraint on an open cubic path (editable in the Rive editor); the cursor's distance is keyed, not x/y
cursor.path_bow_about: max deviation from the straight chord, as a fraction of the chord: a gentle hand arc, every leg bowing to the same side
cursor.pass_about: points the cursor only hovers on the way (a menu row) keep ~30% of the leg's mean speed: it slows, it doesn't stop
cursor.enter_exit: every visit starts and ends off-frame: it arrives already moving (fast start, like 'settle') and leaves accelerating (like (1,0,1,1)); it never appears or vanishes inside the frame
cursor.no_ride: the cursor never travels out with a match-cut exit, or it vanishes on screen at the cut (rule: user review of eComm v8, 'quando o mouse clica, ele some'; the build fails it). After its last click it leaves the frame before the cut, or, when the click opens the next screen, the cut's exit starts on the press and the cursor crosses the cut: the visit has `screen: true` (above the scenes, points in frame coordinates) and leaves from the next scene (rule: user review of eComm v9, 'ao clicar, a transicao ja deve comecar')
cursor.press_lead_about: clicks land a moment before the cursor fully stops: the press starts this many frames before the approach ends (the release ends with the arrival). hero_smb: 4-10 frames
cursor.creep_about: design px/s while the cursor 'thinks' or waits: barely moving (~0.5 px/frame at 1920), never parked

aside.about: Duda's standard for typing into a field: the cursor clicks the field (caret + focus), drifts away on a soft rounded hook (to the side, then curving down toward the bottom-right), turns without stopping, and swoops back so it lands on the next control as the last character is typed. Use the 'away' and 'back' eases; in beats.yaml write {aside: true} between the two clicks and type with `until` (the build places the turn and sets the typing speed).
aside.ease_about: normalised cubic-bezier on the Follow Path distance (x = time, y = progress of the leg). 'away': leaves the click from rest, slow and rounded, still moving when it reaches the turn. 'back': picks up speed, peaks at ~40% and lands very softly into the next click (long flat tail). No pause between them.
aside.ease_source: hero_smb CENA 1.2 ROOT/BG/CURSOR 2, keys MAIN f79/121/166: (0.338,0,0.228,0.0616 of 0.14) and (0.546,0.237,0.061,0.413 over 0.14->0.413), 0.70 s + 0.75 s; the user's reference for this move
aside.turn_offset_about: where the turn sits relative to the click, in design px (680-wide frame): to the right and down. Pulled closer automatically if the swoop back would pass the cursor cap
aside.name: Duda typing pattern
aside.shape_about: arc (default, `{aside: true}`): one simple arc from the clicked field to the next control, bulging away from the text (below it), turn at its midpoint, heading along the chord. hook (`{aside: hook}`): video 1's hook (to the side, then curving back), only when the next control sits behind the field (video 1's '+' was left/below the prompt). User review of video 2: the hook toward a control on the right reads as a strange loop.

cursor.interaction: every control the cursor clicks reacts: hover state ~150 ms before the press, press feedback (scale 0.9-0.96 and/or colour) on the press frame, the result on the press frame

think.about: a short 'thought' on something that opens more options: the cursor slows down over most of the approach (user's curve .61,0,.11,~.91), creeps ~4 px, and eases away gently. 'auto' values are solved so the speed matches the creep on both sides: the value graph has no kinks, only smooth curves and straight lines.
think.source: user review of video 1 (v5): the stop on Connectors felt abrupt; curve given by the user

breath.about: A breath between two clicks, lighter than a 'thought': the cursor never stops. After a click it leaves fast, peaking about 0.3 s after the press. It slows to a crawl at a pass point, at about 20-25% of that peak, then picks up again and lands on the next control with a long, soft deceleration of about 0.75 s. It gives the viewer a beat to follow and reads human. Use it where that helps, not on every visit: in beats.yaml write ease: go on the pass point and ease: land on the next click.
breath.ease_about: normalised cubic-bezier on the Follow Path distance of one leg (x = time, y = progress). 'go': from the click at rest, fast start, long decay into the pass point at ~0.5x the leg's mean speed. 'land': out of the pass point at the leg's mean speed, a short push, then a long settle to rest on the control.
breath.source: videos/ecomm-sep-2026: Mateus's Rive-editor edit of CURSOR_A (toggle -> under the description -> the info icon)

cursor.one_cursor_per_task: when the next action continues the same task in the same scene (open Copilot, then its field), the same cursor travels there; it doesn't leave and come back as another one. Through a push-in it keeps a screen-space path (one simple arc on screen) and grows with the zoom to the designed size (`push ... carry: {CURSOR.size: s}`). User review of video 2.

opacity.source: opacity segments median 34 ms, p75 163 ms: movement carries entrances, opacity only cuts/short fades

speed_cap_px_per_frame_at_1920.source: position peak px/frame p50 7.0, p90 30.8 (rule: cap at p90)

rules_rule.rest_to_rest: anything visible starts and ends at rest RELATIVE TO ITS SCENE CAMERA; fast-start curves ('settle') only where the start is invisible (entering, cut) or the move is <= 60 px
rules_rule.no_ghost: never two dense layers above 15% opacity on the same frame
rules_rule.one_camera_move: one camera action at a time, velocity continuous
rules_rule.loop_seam: the seam is either a hold of >= 8 still frames or a match cut (the video then starts mid-entry)
rules_rule.never_static: some motion on screen at every frame (camera drift at minimum)

match_cut.about: A transition is a hard cut hidden inside one continuous motion: the outgoing scene accelerates (exit) and the incoming scene continues the SAME kind of motion in the SAME direction, decelerating (entry). Not a morph between elements.

entry_speed_ratio.about: first-frame speed of the entry / mean of the exit's last 4 frames

zoom.about: zoom_in / zoom_out cuts are subtler and shorter: the exit scales 10% (110% in, 90% out) in 20 frames; the entry starts 7% away from rest (93% -> 100% in, 107% -> 100% out) and lands in 35 frames. Beats leave out amount and durations so these apply.
zoom.pivot: frame_centre: both scenes of a zoom cut scale about the centre of the frame, so only the scale moves. An off-centre pivot slides the content, and two different pivots make the zoom's centre jump at the cut, read as a position move (rule: user review of eComm v8; the build fails it)
zoom.ratio_about: with a 20-frame exit the 4-frame mean is low (the exit's last frame is ~2x it), so the entry's first frame is ~1.1x that mean while still ~0.6x the exit's last frame: it still lands
zoom.source: rule: user review of eComm v5 (cut 1 -> 2 was 130% in 30 frames, entry 54 frames: 'pra ficar mais sutil')

match_cut.source: hero1 CENA 2->3: zoom out (1,0,1,1) 400 ms | cut | zoom out (0,0,0,1) 967 ms; CENA 3->4: up (1,0,1,1) 1067 ms | cut | up (0,0,0.11,1) 667 ms; measured entry/exit speed ratio 0.34-0.36

camera_drift.about: The camera never stops: each scene keeps a slow constant zoom or pan, usually the continuation of the motion it entered with. Additive to transitions (separate node).
camera_drift.source: hero_smb 'sky' 385 px in 21 s linear; hero1 CENA 4 CTRL GERAL slow scale 1.139 -> 1.197; CENA 5 slow x drifts 2.4-2.9 s (rule: tune by eye)

state_swap.about: one state of an element gives way to the next (loader -> check, icon -> icon): the outgoing state fades out, the incoming one starts on the outgoing state's last visible frame. Never both on screen.

check_draw.about: the check is a trimmed stroke that draws on; its start is invisible, so a fast start is fine

state_swap.source: rule: user review of video 1 (the check arriving while the loader was still visible bothered them)

camera_push.about: In-scene push: the same screen shown at two scales in consecutive storyboard frames (e.g. a panel, then the same panel 2.5x). One continuous camera move on its own node (PUSH_X), never a match cut (identical content on both sides of a cut shows the speed drop as a hiccup).
camera_push.only_when: only when the storyboard itself draws the same screen at two scales. Never to make small text readable, point at a detail or fill time: it crops the designer's composition (rule: user review of eComm v7, 'nao gosto desses zooms, o design fica feio'). Small must-read text is fixed in the storyboard
camera_push.space_about: the ease runs on log(scale), so a big zoom looks even instead of rushing at the start (choreo bakes it as one fitted cubic)
camera_push.pivot: the fixed point between the two frames (where frame A and frame B overlap)
camera_push.rule: the text the viewer reads stays <= text cap; edges leave the frame faster, like a cut exit

ai_rewrite.about: The AI changes existing text: a purple highlight sweeps each line left to right; its edge is the swap boundary (old text to its right, new text to its left, never both on a pixel) and a soft lilac light rides the edge. The AI button lights up while it works. Source first, then where it is shown (editor, then the live preview). The highlight then breathes (a slow shine) while the new text is read.
ai_rewrite.source: rule: video 2 (Copilot), Figma frame 11 highlight (Decorative pallete/bright-purple @70%)
